A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. All 23 pages, including equations, algorithms, figures, tables and Appendices A–D, are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original Gaussian-mixture simulations, image-restoration and class-conditional generation experiments, ablations and sampling analyses, including quantitative and qualitative results in Appendices C–D.

after.justification: v2 retains these original simulations, experiments and analyses in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: AdamDPS, AdamCG and their adaptive-moment updates are unchanged in Section 3 and Algorithms 1–5. No algorithmic component, objective or sampling procedure is revised.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic Gaussian mixture, ImageNet, CIFAR-10 and Cats data, with the same restoration and class-conditional tasks. The new mention of PDEs concerns cited work, not an added evaluation.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged across the corresponding experiments and Tables 1–9. PiGDM and AdamPiGDM are relabeled using the Greek symbol Π in Tables 1 and 3; these are retained methods. Gallon et al. is cited but not evaluated.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendix A retain the same metrics, 32-image validation and 2048-image test sets, 150-trial hyperparameter search, default 100-step DDPM sampling and alternative sampling-budget evaluations.

E4.justification: The synthetic noise study, task-difficulty and sampling-step ablations, moment ablations, timing comparisons and sampling-trajectory analyses are retained without changes to their evidence. Appendix qualitative examples are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report timing averaged over five trials and 25th–75th percentile shading in Figures 9–10. No run-count, seed, uncertainty-reporting or statistical-testing practice changes.

E6.justification: Numerical entries in Tables 1–9 and the plotted and qualitative results are unchanged. Section 5 replaces '9.86%' with '9.86 points' when describing the CIFAR-10 accuracy gap; this clarifies the wording without changing the underlying scores or rankings.

T1.justification: Equations 1–11, the diffusion assumptions and the adaptive-moment formulation are unchanged. Neither version adds or removes a theorem, proof or substantive derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and central conclusion retain the same claims about improved guidance through adaptive moments, minimal overhead and the importance of task difficulty. The removed scientific-domain outlook does not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: Section 7 removes the prospective application to underdetermined inverse problems in scientific domains with sparse, noisy conditioning. Interpretations of noise stabilization, TFG overfitting and task-dependent performance remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation notes, hyperparameter-search details, hardware disclosures and code/model access information are retained. Appendices A–B provide the same experimental details and pseudocode.

R1.justification: Section 6 and the bibliography add Gallon et al. (2026), Physics-informed diffusion models in spectral space. The new sentence acknowledges concurrent application of Adam to DPS for PDEs, providing a limited but directly relevant update to research positioning.

P1.justification: Local edits fix grammar, standardize terminology, clarify accuracy-gap wording and add Jimmy Ba to the Adam citation and reference. Related work and the conclusion receive small edits; section order and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Tables 1 and 3 replace PiGDM/AdamPiGDM labels with ΠGDM/AdamΠGDM, causing small spacing changes. Bibliographic additions also reflow the reference pages. Figures, table organization and appendix image grids are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 improves attribution by acknowledging directly overlapping concurrent work in Section 6 and adding Ba to the Adam reference. Wording and notation corrections provide modest clarity gains. The methods, experimental evidence and reproducibility information remain unchanged, so the overall improvement is limited.
